taxonomyNote: NatureServe calls it Southern Two-lined Salamander; some authorities treat it as a subspecies of Eurycea bislineata.
fieldMarks: Small: about 6-12 cm total length, tail nearly half of total length.
Yellow-orange to rusty body with two dark-brown stripes running its length that break into speckling toward the tail.
Back and often sides speckled with dark-brown spots.
Breeding males grow two cirri, small antenna-like lobes hanging from the snout.
behavior: Cryptic; spends most time under logs or foliage and emerges to forage on the forest floor on damp nights; sometimes active by day in shaded wet areas.
Males may be territorial toward other males.
Often seen crossing roads in rainy weather during the breeding season; eggs are laid on or under submerged rocks, logs or plants, in winter in the south.
habitat: Rocky brooks, springs, seepages, river swamps and forested floodplains with stagnant pools; may disperse into wooded uplands in wet weather.
range: Illinois, Indiana, southern Ohio, western West Virginia and central Virginia south to northern Florida, southern Alabama, southern Mississippi and southeastern Louisiana. Not in Canada.

lookalikes.name: Northern two-lined salamander
lookalikes.howToTell: 15-16 costal grooves; occurs to the north.

lookalikes.name: Dwarf salamander
lookalikes.howToTell: Only four toes on each hind foot.
